units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
} LADY BRITOMART. } Confession! BARBARA. } STEPHEN. }
units.name: SARAH

units.text: Oh I say!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: Yes, a confession. Listen, all. Until I met Barbara I thought myself in the main an honorable, truthful man, because I wanted the approval of my conscience more than I wanted anything else. But the moment I saw Barbara, I wanted her far more than the approval of my conscience.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Adolphus!
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: It is true. You accused me yourself, Lady Brit, of joining the Army to worship Barbara; and so I did. She bought my soul like a flower at a street corner; but she bought it for herself.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: What! Not for Dionysos or another?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Dionysos and all the others are in herself. I adored what was divine in her, and was therefore a true worshipper. But I was romantic about her too. I thought she was a woman of the people, and that a marriage with a professor of Greek would be far beyond the wildest social ambitions of her rank.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Adolphus!!
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: Oh I say!!!
units.name: LOMAX

units.text: When I learnt the horrible truth--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: What do you mean by the horrible truth, pray?
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: That she was enormously rich; that her grandfather was an earl; that her father was the Prince of Darkness--
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Chut!
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: --and that I was only an adventurer trying to catch a rich wife, then I stooped to deceive about my birth.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Your birth! Now Adolphus, don't dare to make up a wicked story for the sake of these wretched cannons. Remember: I have seen photographs of your parents; and the Agent General for South Western Australia knows them personally and has assured me that they are most respectable married people.
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: So they are in Australia; but here they are outcasts. Their marriage is legal in Australia, but not in England. My mother is my father's deceased wife's sister; and in this island I am consequently a foundling.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Sensation.
Is the subterfuge good enough, Machiavelli?
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [thoughtfully] Biddy: this may be a way out of the difficulty.
Stuff! A man can't make cannons any the better for being his own cousin instead of his proper self
units.name: LADY BRITOMART

units.text: she sits down in the deck chair with a bounce that expresses her downright contempt for their casuistry.
UNDERSHAFT [to Cusins] You are an educated man.
That is against the tradition.

Once in ten thousand times it happens that the schoolboy is a born master of what they try to teach him. Greek has not destroyed my mind: it has nourished it. Besides, I did not learn it at an English public school.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Hm! Well, I cannot afford to be too particular: you have cornered the foundling market. Let it pass. You are eligible, Euripides: you are eligible.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: BARBARA [coming from the platform and interposing between Cusins and Undershaft] Dolly: yesterday morning, when Stephen told us all about the tradition, you became very silent; and you have been strange and excited ever since.
Were you thinking of your birth then?
When the finger of Destiny suddenly points at a man in the middle of his breakfast, it makes him thoughtful.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Barbara turns away sadly and stands near her mother, listening perturbedly.
Aha! You have had your eye on the business, my young friend, have you?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Take care! There is an abyss of moral horror between me and your accursed aerial battleships.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Never mind the abyss for the present. Let us settle the practical details and leave your final decision open. You know that you will have to change your name. Do you object to that?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: Would any man named Adolphus--any man called Dolly!--object to be called something else?
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Good. Now, as to money! I propose to treat you handsomely from the beginning. You shall start at a thousand a year.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: with sudden heat, his spectacles twinkling with mischief.

A thousand! You dare offer a miserable thousand to the son-in-law of a millionaire! No, by Heavens, Machiavelli! you shall not cheat me. You cannot do without me; and I can do without you. I must have two thousand five hundred a year for two years. At the end of that time, if I am a failure, I go. But if I am a success, and stay on, you must give me the other five thousand.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: What other five thousand?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: To make the two years up to five thousand a year. The two thousand five hundred is only half pay in case I should turn out a failure. The third year I must have ten per cent on the profits.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: UNDERSHAFT [taken aback] Ten per cent!
Why, man, do you know what my profits are?
Enormous, I hope: otherwise I shall require twenty-five per cent.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: But, Mr Cusins, this is a serious matter of business. You are not bringing any capital into the concern.
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: What! no capital! Is my mastery of Greek no capital? Is my access to the subtlest thought, the loftiest poetry yet attained by humanity, no capital? my character! my intellect! my life! my career! what Barbara calls my soul! are these no capital? Say another word; and I double my salary.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Be reasonable--
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: CUSINS [peremptorily] Mr Undershaft: you have my terms.
Take them or leave them.
UNDERSHAFT [recovering himself] Very well.
I note your terms; and I offer you half.
CUSINS [disgusted] Half!
UNDERSHAFT [firmly] Half.
